speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, we thank Members for all their suggestions and comments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In particular, the passionate speech by Ms Denise Phua and the vivid imagery of Mr Patrick Tay's Iron Man.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To Ms Phua, I would like to share that indeed new wine needs new wineskins, not just one type but many types, to cater to the diversity of needs and aspirations of our people.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: More importantly, we need new mindsets, which I will come back to, together with Mr Patrick Tay's Iron Man.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Like the public, some Members have asked the Ministry of Education (MOE) to do less.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They are calling for later start times and earlier end times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They believe in teach less, test less, less stress and hopefully, better results for all.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They want smaller class sizes, smaller schools, closer guidance and supervision, better support for students with higher needs and more types of learning opportunities; including Ms Carrie Tan, who suggested incorporating more nature and outdoor experiences into the curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many Members have given us suggestions on what more we should teach in our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I was hoping to also hear more views on what we can remove from our students' and teachers' load.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some have called for more porosity in our education pathways, more social mixing in schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Others want affiliation priority and alumni privileges to be maintained, to build stronger school networks and uphold their school culture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some have called for the removal of Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE), others to extend PSLE preparations for our students to more overseas schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some have called for smaller school sizes, more niche programmes and co-curricular activities (CCA).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Others think every school should be able to offer a comprehensive and identical suite of programmes and CCA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ultimately, we all have to work within the finite resources and time budget of our school system, students, teachers and even parents, to best meet the needs of diverse needs of our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Every idea is well-meaning but it affects different groups of stakeholders differently.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To chart our way forward, we have to first understand the complex needs of the future and the diverse needs of our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: A more diverse population with diverse aspirations demands mass customisation beyond mass access.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We should expect a more variegated system, with more models, but within our means and capabilities and a less structured system to allow adaptation and faster evolution.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are starting from a position of strength.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These students typically have less access to private tuition and have still managed to do well by international standards.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This goes to show that our students are industrious and our education system is doing something right.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead of attributing our students' achievements to the private tuition industry, we should give credit to our students, schools and teachers where credit is due.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In recent years, our efforts to support our students to progress to our post-secondary education institutions have also been paying off.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nonetheless, we will be the first to acknowledge that our system is not perfect.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, I do not believe that there will ever be "perfection" for our system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Adaptability, resilience and relevance to the times are much more important attributes and we certainly will not sit on our laurels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I have covered the larger philosophical and directional issues of our education system at the Institute of Policy Studies' Singapore Perspectives 2023 seminar.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Members can read the speech online and I do not intend to repeat them today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, today, let me walk Members through the challenges and aspirations for each stage of our education journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We start by giving every child a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There is more scientific evidence and we all agree that the foundational years play a critical role in our children's holistic development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond numeracy and literacy, this is also when they develop important socio-emotional skills and their innate curiosity to learn.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Hence, we have taken decisive steps to make affordable and high-quality preschool education accessible to families.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are on track to opening another seven by 2025 and a further three by 2027 based on current plans.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, around 95% of all Singaporean children aged five to six years old are enrolled in preschools, even without making it compulsory under the law.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, among children from the lower-income families, we still see an enrolment gap at ages three to four, and poorer attendance compared to their peers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to go beyond enrolment to encourage regular attendance.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: More importantly, we need to work with families to create conducive home environments which can help our children's development so that all these efforts will complement and not undo the good work of our preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We know that there is no silver bullet in addressing these complex family and social issues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Government provides targeted assistance to lower-income families based on their individual circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This includes supporting them in their parenting journey through KidSTART and highly subsidising the cost of preschool.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Together with the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), we welcome more ideas on how preschools, families and the community can work together to better support children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Next, for primary schools, let me deal with three issues: Primary 1 (P1) registration, affiliation and PSLE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Louis Chua asked about the P1 Registration Exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Parents consider various factors in selecting primary schools for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some parents prefer convenience for a school near their homes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Others would like their children to join their alma mater, so they can benefit from a similar school experience and become part of the same school community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yet, others place a premium on the types of programmes offered by a school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While MOE can guarantee more than sufficient places for all Singapore Citizen children in our primary schools, no one has yet found a way to satisfy all parental preferences.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The P1 Registration Framework has to strike a careful balance among the competing considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We revised the framework last year and we will continue to update the system as circumstances change and societal needs evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: More importantly, we need to promote a mindset shift among us parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Every child is unique in his or her temperament, strengths and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead of asking whether a certain school is a good school, the more relevant question to ask is, "Is this a good school for my child?" As parents, we should choose schools based on our children's needs, rather than the perceived prestige or popularity of the school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Members have also discussed the educational merits of school affiliation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It enables a school to preserve its traditions and culture, and build a stronger school spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But affiliation, beyond a certain point, is not without its risks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to avoid closed and exclusive social circles, which risk fragmenting and stratifying our society, especially as our society matures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This means we must ensure that schools with affiliation remain open, accessible and inclusive for students of diverse backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This balance to maintain the accessibility of our schools to all, regardless of background, is a dynamic balance that we must be prepared to adjust over time according to our societal circumstances and needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE cannot do this alone without the support of school alumni and parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The privileged, among us, must believe in sharing their access and networks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must understand the responsibilities that come with success and not inadvertently form closed social circles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As Spiderman would say, "To those with great powers, come great responsibilities." And I hope that all the alumni from the successful schools understand what I mean.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Moving on to PSLE, there are calls to remove the PSLE, but for different reasons – all well-meaning, but not always without unintended consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But it is neither realistic nor desirable to shield our children from all the stresses they will have to face in life, especially in a more competitive and globalised world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our job as parents and educators is to help our children pick up the skills and positive attributes and attitudes to manage the demands of school, work and life in general; to grow our capacity to overcome stress and not just to shield ourselves from unnecessary stress.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We should not demoralise our children through incessant comparison.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This encourages students to focus on their own progress instead of comparing themselves with others.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why in all my Edusave Awards Ceremony, I remind the students that "it is more important to keep surpassing oneself through life than just surpassing someone else in an exam".

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have also received feedback that removing the PSLE would allow our children to pursue other dimensions of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Besides reducing the assessment load and perceived examination stakes, these adjustments free up more time and space in schools to strengthen learning dispositions and holistic development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some Members, including Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Ms Hazel Poa and Ms Denise Phua, in previous years, have brought up the related concept of through-train programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, we have studied this issue very carefully in MOE but there are various implications to work through.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The PSLE is a useful guide for students to take subjects at appropriate levels at the next stage of learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Without the PSLE, it would be more challenging to place students in a suitable educational setting and not always better for learning outcomes, nor teaching efficacy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, many parents and students would like to choose their schools or educational setting.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For this group, removing the PSLE entirely would deny them this choice, or simply transfer stress elsewhere, such as to competition for P1 registration.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In simple terms, few would hesitate if the through-train programme helps their children get into a popular secondary school.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But many would hesitate if it means they do not have a choice to be in a secondary school of their choice through merit.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We should also consider if a through-train model would reduce opportunities for students to interact with peers of different backgrounds through their primary and secondary years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are other ways to support the learning needs of different students flexibly, without completely doing away with national examinations or moving entirely to a through-train system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yet, another example is Subject-Based Banding (SBB), which Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Darryl David have asked for updates on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond reducing stigmatisation, the removal of course labels will lead to meaningful changes in our students' educational journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students will have greater flexibility to take subjects at a level that is more or less demanding, depending on their strengths, interests and learning needs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There will be more social mixing, with increased opportunities for students to interact with peers of different profiles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, it is not a straightforward transition for schools to make.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Teachers will need to get used to managing classes with diverse student profiles.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is actually more work and harder work for our teachers and schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our teachers are willing to do this for the benefit of our students, but we should not think that it does not demand more from our teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students will need to take greater ownership of their learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our schools also have to grapple with the practical issues such as timetable scheduling for various subject combinations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE will carefully and systematically work through these issues to support our schools in the implementation of FSBB and provide them with the necessary resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, if we accept that our children have different abilities and needs, then we should accept that we should not make every school take the same approach to teaching and learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why we have a variegated education landscape today.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Schools offering the Integrated Programme and Specialised Schools will not implement the full features of FSBB because they cater to specific student profiles through a whole-school approach.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Homogenising all our schools for the sake of social mixing alone would come at the expense of our ability to offer mass customisation and differentiated experiences for our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I do not think this is the outcome that Members want from us.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nonetheless, we have sought to enhance diversity in our schools through other means, while moving away from the sole dependence on the national examination as a single metric for placement to secondary schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This includes our efforts to increase the proportion of students admitted via Direct School Admission (DSA) system and broadening the definition of DSA selection process to recognise a range of talents, potential and achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The vast majority of students will continue to be admitted to secondary schools based on their PSLE scores.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This ensures that schools continue to admit students with diverse strengths and students continue to have access to a wide range of schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: By admitting students from different Posting Groups, schools can also enable diversity at the class level, with mixed form classes that comprise students offering subjects at different subject levels.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Unlike streaming, Posting Groups will only be used to facilitate admissions and to determine students' initial subject levels for most subjects at the beginning of Secondary 1.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond that, Posting Groups will not shape the secondary school experience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Currently, students may choose to take certain subjects at a more demanding level if they are eligible.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Under Full Subject-Based Banding (FSBB), this flexibility has been expanded to more subjects.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With guidance from their schools, some students have also begun to offer elective subjects at a less demanding level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This gives them room to pursue their interests without adding unduly stress to their overall curriculum load.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The option of spending a fifth year in secondary school will remain available to students who wish to offer subjects at a more demanding level.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is to allow them to pace their learning and potentially access more post-secondary pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Students should still have strong fundamentals to thrive in the pathways they choose.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Hence, we will be retaining the existing junior college admission criteria to ensure students can cope with the A-Level curriculum.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Darryl David asked if MOE plans to review the "A" Level curriculum, to ensure that it remains relevant in today's education landscape.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Over the years, we have gradually reduced curriculum content to free up more time and space for the development of 21st Century Competencies, or 21CC, as we call it.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, the curriculum content of most of our "A" Level syllabus is already similar or narrower than the international syllabus used as benchmarks, for comparison.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not possible to reduce curriculum content further without compromising the overall rigour.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, we will be making key changes in other ways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, Project Work (PW) nurtures 21CC and life skills through working in teams.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are the very skills which Members have said are essential to thrive in the future of work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our students have done well in PW over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Making PW a Pass/Fail subject now encourages our students to exercise greater agency and creativity in areas of interests, rather than be driven by grades alone.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, to nurture the joy of learning, we want our students to follow their passions, instead of only picking subjects that they will score well in.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To achieve this, we will make changes to how we compute the University Admissions System (UAS).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will also allow our students to better calibrate their learning load, so that more time can be redirected to holistic development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I should emphasise that students will continue to benefit from a broad-based "A" Level curriculum, as they still have to offer four content-based subjects, of which one would be from outside their specialisation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Parents and educators may be concerned that our pre-tertiary students will no longer take their fourth content-based subject or PW seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We believe that our students will still apply themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, it is already optional for students taking H1 Mother Tongue Language (MTL) to include the subject in their UAS computation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nevertheless, these students continue to put effort towards their MTL studies as they are intrinsically motivated to learn and improve.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And this is exactly the positive attitude that we hope to cultivate through our curriculum changes – with students taking ownership of their own learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The time saved from preparing for examinations can be channelled towards deeper student engagement and learning through more varied experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Teachers will continue to use assessments in a formative and calibrated way to monitor learning progress and support each student.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The removal of the Mid-Year Examinations will take place in phases for different levels in junior colleges and MI starting from 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our efforts to foster stronger 21CC development and ensure future-ready graduates extend to our IHLs as well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Sharael Taha highlighted that companies value industry-relevant skills and competencies over paper qualifications.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our IHLs equip students with life skills competencies, such as critical thinking, innovation, communication, as well as self-awareness and mental resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Part of the training in IHLs also includes developing interdisciplinary expertise, which means that students learn to apply knowledge and skills across different fields.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For instance, under the new Minor programme launched by Republic Polytechnic this year, students can embark on additional areas of study beyond their diploma, such as in Business, Digitalisation or Sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Denise Phua noted that in the 2016 OECD Survey of Adult Skills, Singaporeans aged 16 to 34 performed well, while those aged 45 to 65 performed lower than the OECD average in literacy and numeracy.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is a reflection of how OECD countries have built up their education systems much earlier than us and their older cohorts have benefitted from this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For Singapore, we should take heart that we have done a tremendous job in bringing our schools and higher education system to high standards within the span of the past few decades.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why the performance of our younger Singaporeans were comparable with the advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: With lifelong learning, we are now doing more for both our young and young-at-heart, as what we teach and learn in the first 15 years is no longer adequate for the next 50 years, without a significant top-up.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In fact, given the rapid pace of industry transformation, we can expect more dynamic changes in the demand for skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, Members have also raised concerns about perpetuating a paper chase.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The objective of continual learning must be the purposeful and timely acquisition of relevant knowledge and skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When a certain defined body of knowledge or skills has been acquired, the qualification then serves to reflect the mastery attained.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The stackable pathways that our IHLs have significantly expanded in recent years enable this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, there are pathways offering substantive skills upgrading at different levels catering to Nitec, Diploma and Degree holders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will ensure that training opportunities continue to be industry-relevant, accessible, affordable and just-in-time, to better meet the needs of our adult learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Today, we have a 40% lifetime cohort participation rate target for subsidised undergraduate degree places for fresh school leavers, and an additional 10% allowance for adult learners.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This takes into account the demand for degree-level manpower across the economy in the medium term, arising from our industry transformation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The move to a "lifetime cohort participation rate" concept symbolises the change in mindset that we need to embrace.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There is no need to rush to frontload education, as there will be more subsidised places for CET pathways to support upgrading later in life.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is also about ensuring that the format of these CET programmes is suited to the needs of our working adults and to the industries that they work in.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The AUs have begun to innovate their offerings to better cater to adult learners' needs as well.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mid-career workers looking to switch into the ICT sector can pursue a degree in Applied Computing at the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) whilst working.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The degree programme will be delivered through a mixture of asynchronous and in-person learning to help adult learners manage their busy schedules.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Individuals who are already working in the ICT sector can deepen their skills or pick up new specialisations through SIT's micro-credentials.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These are modular courses which deliver job-related skills in areas, such as Computer Networks and Software Engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: They can also stack these micro-credentials towards the Applied Computing degree.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Alternatively, individuals who prefer a more skills-based upgrading pathway can sign up for the 42-Singapore Programme in Computing, a collaboration between Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) and École 42.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There are no academic prerequisites, and students will undergo industry-relevant training centred on project-based and peer-to-peer learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE is also studying how to better support mid-career workers by enabling them to upskill ahead of job transitions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In the past year, under the Forward Singapore exercise, we heard from Singaporeans on the barriers to reskilling or upskilling, particularly for those in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are looking at ways to reduce the high opportunity costs of training for this group of workers, to enable them to participate in more substantive training for a skills reboot.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: However, to achieve lifelong learning, just shifting individual attitudes and raising the supply of training programmes will not be enough if employers continue to fixate on credentials.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need employers to hire and compensate workers fairly, based on their skills rather than paper qualifications, support workers in their upskilling and provide opportunities for workers to apply new skills at work.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will ensure that after undergoing training, Singaporeans can get a real boost to their employability and wages, and access to better job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chairman, I have talked about providing customised and porous pathways for continual learning across the life course.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Three key enablers undergird this vision: technology, educators and partnership.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Technology is altering every aspect of life, and education is no exception.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Technology has raised the productivity in our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have, and will, continue to digitise and streamline manual processes with the use of Parents Gateway, a one-stop portal for schools to communicate with parents.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This has helped to alleviate teachers' admin workload.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But as Mr Darryl David, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Dr Wan Rizal have observed, the potential of the EdTech Plan goes beyond that.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have seen how technology allowed learning to continue across all schools even through the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: EdTech also allows for mass customisation of teaching and learning, catering to the diverse learning needs of our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These have been enabled by our national online learning platform – the Singapore Student Learning Space (SLS).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Members may also access these materials through the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The screenshot shows the SLS resource library, where students can learn a range of academic subjects from primary school to pre-university, as well as to explore their non-academic topics, such as financial literacy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students can access these online resources via SLS anytime, anywhere.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I am quite sure most parents do not know this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, students can use simulations and interactives to visualise concepts which might otherwise be hard to grasp.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, the movement of individual particles in a wave or the relationship between distance and time illustrated by the movement of a train.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: With SLS, all our students have effectively been equipped with a "personal tutor"; that is, a wealth of resources and tools to guide their individual learning, no matter their financial resources.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The screenshot which we had distributed is meant as a taster for the parents amongst us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I hope that Members will find time tonight to log in with your children to explore its many useful features.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is a friendly cost-saving tip for all parents; no need to go and buy other school exam papers and try our SLS for free.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Imagine the future of learning augmented by EdTech, where our higher-needs students can identify and improve their areas of weaknesses by revisiting lessons and resources at their own pace, and higher-ability students can stretch themselves by progressing to more advanced topics or topics that interest them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This mass customisation uplifts the bottom and stretches the top without overloading our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To give an example, the Learning Feedback Assistant for English Language will provide basic and personalised feedback on grammar and spelling to students, allowing our teachers to focus on more complex aspects of language use, such as creative expression and tone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will share more about our long-term EdTech plans in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, MOE already takes a two-pronged approach in supporting our students' diverse learning needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, we put more resources where the needs are higher.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools have the flexibility to deploy teachers to teach students with higher needs in smaller pull-out classes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, we focus on recruiting and training competent educators to ensure that our students receive high-quality education.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the future, we can add a third prong to capitalise on EdTech to further enable self-directed and adaptive learning, to better support our students with different needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As EdTech becomes a pivotal part in our strategy to support the diverse learning needs of our students, our teachers must also grow and be conversant with EdTech.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE will continue to support our teachers with training and resources to develop their capacity to teach with technology.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers will learn more about pedagogies that lend themselves better deliver the 21CC gain digital literacy as well as content and skills related to STEM and environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, educators are the backbone of our education system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Rest assured that we will not tolerate any abuse towards our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have provided schools with clear guidelines on establishing positive home-school partnerships.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I hope to have everyone's support to respect the professionalism of our teachers and not create undue stress for our teachers when they do not fulfil our individual demands.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Supporting our educators in focusing on higher value tasks and providing them with opportunities for professional development are some other ways in which MOE supports the well-being of our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Parent Support Groups (PSGs) have been active partners in enhancing our students' educational experience, such as in the area of Education and Career Guidance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For instance, in Palm View Primary School, the PSG invites parents in diverse occupations to share with the students about their work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Such collaborations help our students better understand their interests and aspirations, as well as the range of careers available.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Alumni also play an important role in plugging students and fresh graduates into industry networks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, SMU's Alumni Mentoring Programme provides a platform for students and graduates to gain insights into specific industries and discover job opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I call on companies and unions to work closely with our IHLs and schools to help our people keep up-to-date with the fast-paced industry developments and emerging opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We share responsibility in preparing our students for the workforce and inspiring the next generation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some companies have partnered our schools to broaden students' exposure through the Applied Learning Programmes (ALPs).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, as part of Dunearn Secondary School's ALP in STEM, food scientists from Fraser & Neave (F&N) Ltd conducted a workshop for interested students to learn about processes behind the creation of new drinks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The F&N food scientists have also been conducting annual Food Science career talks for the graduating students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I hope to see more of such partnerships.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is a win-win situation when companies and unions are directly involved in the training and development of IHL students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Minister Mohamad Maliki Osman will now elaborate on MOE's other policies and I promise to Mr Patrick Tay that I will come back to Iron Man before we conclude.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, MOE is committed to bringing out the best in every student and support them to their full potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As our education system evolves to keep pace with global developments, we must pay special attention to students with greater needs and ensure that they have the opportunities and resilience to grow up well, regardless of their starting point in life and the challenges that they face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Mr Shawn Huang and Ms He Ting Ru pointed out, some students from disadvantaged families find it harder to keep up in school due to their home circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This may lead to long-term absenteeism issues, struggles with motivation and lower self-esteem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To safeguard social mobility and ensure that these students receive the support and develop resilience to overcome challenges in spite of their difficult home circumstances, we established the "Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce" (UPLIFT) in 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2020, we piloted the UPLIFT Community Network (UCN) to strengthen the support ecosystem for students from disadvantaged families and address school attendance issues early.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the pilot showed positive outcomes, I updated Members last year that the UCN will be rolled out nationwide progressively from 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Daania was a Secondary 4 student who skipped school frequently and felt disengaged from her teachers and peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She has five other siblings, including a newborn.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am very sure Members would have seen such cases in their respective constituencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With her father being the sole breadwinner and mother juggling child-minding responsibilities, Daania did not have a good relationship with her parents as they found it difficult to set aside the time and energy to engage and support her.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite Daania's attendance issues, her teachers continued to reach out to her and to encourage her to attend school more regularly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The school also offered financial and academic support to help her cope.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The UCN complements the school's efforts in two ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the Town Level-Coordinator in the UCN ropes in community resources to provide supplementary support to students' educational and developmental needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Daania was also enrolled in the MENDAKI's Tuition Scheme, where she also received additional academic and mentoring support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, the Town-Level Coordinator supports parents to improve and stabilise the home environment, including having volunteer family befrienders mentor these families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With the relaxation of the COVID-19 restrictions, befrienders resumed in-person visits from June last year, allowing them to better connect with their families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In Daania's case, the Coordinator worked with two befrienders to provide Daania's mother with emotional and financial support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The befrienders helped Daania's mother with the childcare application for the youngest child, freeing her to better support her other children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With their support and advice, the relationship between Daania and her mother improved tremendously.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Daania also regained motivation and confidence in her studies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Her school attendance improved and she did well enough to progress to a course of her choice in ITE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The term has started for a few months now and I am glad that she is coping well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Stories like this illustrate how collaboration between schools, families and the community can benefit our students for those who need help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Parents share that they felt more supported by the UCN, appreciate the increased community support and have seen positive developments in their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, beyond the UCN, many community partners have stepped forward to support and befriend students from disadvantaged backgrounds under UPLIFT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, we partnered the Singapore Management University (SMU)'s Centre for Social Responsibilities to pilot befriending programmes for primary school students in need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SMU students and schools co-created activities that served to build students' motivation and resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are grateful for the help of our community partners and will strengthen our partnerships with the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To strengthen the support provided to disadvantaged and at-risk students within the school environment, we have also provided additional manpower resourcing to schools through the UPLIFT Enhanced School Resourcing initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These additional resourcing support schools in establishing more targeted programmes for students with higher needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, some teachers have been deployed to provide mentoring and additional academic support for students with absenteeism issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is in addition to existing programmes like the Learning Support Programme for English (LSP) and the Learning Support for Mathematics (LSM) for lower primary students who need additional support in these subjects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also continue to work closely with other Government agencies to explore how best to strengthen whole-of-Government social service delivery for higher-needs students and those coming from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will include further integrating our processes with other social service initiatives, like ComLink and KidSTART, so that students and their families receive more coordinated and seamless support from the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to our UPLIFT efforts, MOE provides education subsidies and financial support to ensure that our national schools and institutes of higher learning (IHLs) remain accessible and affordable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This ensures that no Singaporean student is unable to access schools and IHLs because of financial reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked if we could extend financial assistance to non-citizen students studying in national schools with at least one SC parent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Financial subsidies are differentiated by students' citizenship status to reflect the benefits of citizenship, in line with the broader Government policy of differentiating benefits by citizenship status.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE will assess their situation and exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis, with special consideration given to those from lower-income households.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Faisal Manap also asked if MOE's financial assistance scheme and Edusave Awards, currently only available to SCs in national schools, can be extended to madrasah students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is not the first time that he has made this point and this will not be the first time that MOE is giving this very considerate response.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This reflects our preference for all SCs to enrol in national schools, to go through a common educational experience so as to build a national identity and social cohesion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Parents are aware and thus make informed choices when they decide to enrol their children in private schools instead of our national schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Notwithstanding, the Government recognises the role of madrasahs in the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS provides financial assistance and alternative awards for madrasah students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, MUIS assists madrasah students from low-income families through the Progress Fund Madrasah Assistance Scheme (PROMAS) and administers the Madrasah Student Awards to recognise academic excellence and progress.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to enable them to lead meaningful lives and fulfil their aspirations despite their learning difficulties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The challenges faced by families and students with SEN are multifaceted and require whole-of-community support across life stages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE works closely with various Government agencies and SSAs to meet the children’s and families’ needs at different stages of their journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will focus on the schooling years today and my Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) colleagues will share more on the additional support that will be provided beyond the school setting.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I want to tell them we hear you.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We feel you and we are with you.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, over the years, we have enhanced SEN support in the education landscape significantly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And we will continue to explore what more we can do with our partners to support our students with SEN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are committed to strengthening structures and teacher capacity for consistent enactment of inclusive practices across all our mainstream schools, in order to lower the barriers to learning and help our students with SEN build key life skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, our schools are supported with teachers trained in special needs and SEN officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These educators are guided by a dedicated case management team that monitors students’ progress and overall well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They work closely with parents to develop holistic intervention plans, and support students’ transition at different stages of their educational journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Schools have also worked hard to grow an inclusive culture where peers actively appreciate and support each other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These friendships bring joy and teach students with SEN how to build meaningful relationships and thrive in school and in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The IHLs similarly provide targeted support for students with SEN, from pre-enrolment to graduation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes course advisement for prospective students, helping students identify courses that better suit their interests and learning needs, and partnering educators to support students’ learning needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The IHLs also work with SSAs to prepare and ease students’ transition to internship and employment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to work with schools and IHLs to strengthen support for our students with SEN across their educational journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, with growing emphasis in education to recognise diverse strengths among our students and the vision for an inclusive Singapore, a key focus is to help peers from diverse profiles integrate and learn from each other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2007, under Satellite Partnerships, SPED schools have been partnering General Education (Gen Ed) schools to conduct joint learning activities, such as learning journeys and camps.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These activities promote inclusion between students with and without SEN, build capabilities for peer support and inculcate positive values.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Besides providing students with opportunities to develop deeper relationships through sustained and meaningful interactions, School Partnerships, that is, between Gen Ed and SPED schools, will also focus on professional exchange between teachers and build capabilities, something suggested by Ms Denise Phua in her speech yesterday.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such mutual professional learning can enhance pedagogical practices in the classroom and strengthen how teachers facilitate integration between students from partner schools to nurture them into empathetic, confident and independent learners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: An example of a successful partnership is between Bukit Merah Secondary School and Tanglin School.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Partners since 2018, students from both schools share their passion for sports and co-curricular activities (CCAs) together through training sessions jointly organised by their teachers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Sudip from Bukit Merah Secondary School shared in his reflections that he learnt how to better work in a team and tap on one another’s strengths through floorball practices with peers from Tanglin School.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Likewise, James from Tanglin School shared that having the opportunity to train with peers from Bukit Merah Secondary School for the Play Inclusive Badminton matches brought them closer and taught him how to work alongside peers new to him.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am heartened by the inclusivity shown by these students and the friendships formed over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will work closely with Gen Ed and SPED schools to develop more meaningful partnerships by finding synergy through shared strategic directions, niche offerings and location proximity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, MOE will continue to enhance the quality of teaching and learning in SPED schools to prepare students to be active in the community and contributing citizens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2020, we have embarked on developing SPED Teaching and Learning Syllabus across seven SPED learning domains to raise the quality of curriculum in SPED schools and to provide them with greater resources to achieve the desired SPED outcomes, including lifelong learning for our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These syllabuses have strengthened curriculum design and lesson delivery, and promoted stronger collaboration between educators and allied professionals, and partnerships with families and the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the Communication and Language syllabus will be launched, and they will place stronger emphasis on communication and strengthen the partnership between teachers and Speech and Language Therapists to equip students with skills to connect meaningfully with others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The second one, the Social-Emotional Learning syllabus will introduce skills of self-determination to give students’ agency in pursuing their aspirations, and nurture confidence and resilience to cope with challenges and changes in their lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These are important life skills to better support students with SEN in their transition to post-school as they integrate with the larger community, help them live independently, learn continuously and work productively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Alongside these curriculum enhancements, we recognise the need to continue working with schools to build capacity and develop the skills of educators to support the implementation of these syllabuses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also continue to deepen our partnerships with SSAs to attract talents and study the suggestions by Members to keep SPED schools forward looking.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked whether the formal SPED school exit age can be extended from 18 to 21 years old.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These students can access open and paid employment, and so a longer runway of up to 21 years old is given to them to attain these national certifications.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For a majority of SPED students, we have pegged the exit age at 18 years old taking into consideration that a post-school option would be more meaningful in supporting their transition from school to community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, for all SPED graduates, MOE is committed to working with SG Enable and the SSAs to facilitate their post-school transition, and to co-create avenues for continual supports for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We fully appreciate the effort of all our SPED schools in equipping our students with skills to prepare them to lead independent and fruitful lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It has not been an easy journey, but we have made significant progress.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE will continually enhance our support for SPED schools, and more details will be shared at upcoming platforms this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, aside from targeted support and programmes, we want to develop resilience in all our students, for them to persevere in the challenges that will inevitably come.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is not easy being a youth in today’s complex and fast-paced environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our youths face pressure on multiple fronts, including on social media.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many youths have spoken up and expressed concerns on mental health issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, many of us when we meet young people at our engagement sessions, key of their mind is really mental health issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And Dr Wan Rizal also spoke on the importance of supporting our students’ mental well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We would like to assure our students and parents that mental well-being will always be a key priority for MOE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past few years, aside from systemic changes to reduce overemphasis on academic grades and to nurture a joy for learning, we have strengthened measures to help students stay resilient amidst challenges and enhanced the overall system of support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the refreshed Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum provides greater emphasis on Mental Health Education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The curriculum aims to help students tap on their natural strengths and develop a wider repertoire of skills and habits so that they can overcome the hurdles that they face, whether at home or in school or in the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These resilience and social-emotional skills are further practised and reinforced beyond the classroom, such as through CCAs and camps.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I encourage all students to make good use of these platforms and develop deeper bonds with your friends who will walk with you through the good and bad times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These educative efforts also extend to the IHLs where there already are a good range of programmes in place to raise awareness on mental health issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we have strengthened the support ecosystem for our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All schools have peer support structures, and students are taught how to look out for, offer support to their peers and refer them to trusted adults where necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Struggling students manifest their distress in different ways, such as social withdrawal or acting out behaviours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Teachers are equipped to look out for these signs of distress and understand underlying needs so that they can provide the right support and guidance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also enhancing mental health literacy to enable teachers to better identify and support students of all ages with mental health struggles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students who need professional support will also be referred to community resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These efforts ensure that early identification of students with mental health issues and that support will be provided in a timely manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond these school-based initiatives, we need strong partnerships with stakeholders, including parents, community partners and agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, I encourage parents to actively journey together with their children and schools to facilitate a more holistic development for their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE is involved in inter-agency collaborative efforts such as the Interagency Taskforce for Mental Health and Well-Being to better support the mental health needs of families, children and youths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One area that the Taskforce is looking into is identifying ways to help youths and parents better access coordinated mental health services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOH will share more details on these efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar and Dr Wan Rizal on the need for our applied education pathways to support the growing interests and learner profiles among our youth.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In January 2022, I announced the recommendations from the Review of Opportunities and Pathways in Applied Education, which studied how to better support the diverse needs and aspirations of students and graduates from the polytechnics and ITE while ensuring that they have the relevant skills to thrive in the future economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Good progress has been made in two key areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Interim indicators from the first phase of implementation have been positive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More students indicated interest for courses under the enhanced curricular structure compared to similar past Nitec courses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Lecturers also observed that students enrolled in the three-year courses are more motivated and attrition rates in the first six months have improved.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students can look forward to courses such as the three-year Higher Nitec in Nursing and International Logistics, which will be launched next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, in recognition of the growing diversity in students' interests and learner profiles, the polytechnics are piloting flexible modular loads.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under this pilot, students can spread their learning beyond three years by taking fewer modules per semester.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such flexibility allows students to pursue other interests and take more time to build their academic foundation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to this pilot, students are given the flexibility to take up electives, where feasible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With limited curriculum hours, institutions have to balance between allocating time for electives and for equipping students with the necessary specialised skill sets and knowledge to meet industry needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE will work closely with the polytechnics and ITE to monitor the progress of these enhancements and make necessary adjustments to ensure they fulfil their intent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As mentioned by Minister Chan Chun Sing, the Full Subject-Based Banding (FSBB) will be fully implemented in secondary schools for the Secondary 1 cohort from next year onwards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a significant move in our overall general education landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With this move, students can customise their learning by taking a combination of subjects at different levels, suited to their strengths and pace of learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In line with this shift, MOE will adjust the admissions criteria for post-secondary pathways to recognise more diverse profiles of learners and provide them with more options.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The range of post-secondary pathways that students could be eligible for will no longer be limited by streams but by their performance at different subject levels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, more students will be able to access the Polytechnic Foundation Programme (PFP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, the PFP is only open to eligible students from the Normal (Academic) stream.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, students are admitted directly to specific diplomas in their PFP year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2026, students will be admitted to broad clusters such as sciences and humanities, arts, media and business before choosing a specific diploma in the cluster after their PFP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Students will have more time to make informed choices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Polytechnics can also better match students' interest and abilities with specific diplomas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This builds on our efforts to expose students to multiple courses in a cluster before deciding on a specific diploma that they want to pursue, an approach currently adopted by the Common Entry Programmes in the polytechnics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, MOE will review admissions to Polytechnic Year 1 to better recognise the different subject levels taken by students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, today, students have to take five G3 subjects to be eligible for Polytechnic Year 1.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With FSBB, some may take subjects at the G2 level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are exploring allowing one G2 subject to be considered for admission.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to these enhancements, ITE students will have more opportunities and flexibility to determine their skills and competencies through the expansion of ITE diploma offerings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These offerings will enable students to better attain work-ready skills in line with changing industry needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE's Work-Study Diplomas (WSDips) and Technical Diplomas (TDs) are apprenticeship-based, which cater to students who prefer a more hands-on learning style.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: WSDips also place students in jobs related to their discipline of study, allowing them to deepen their skills through a structured training programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus far, about 1,600 students have graduated from ITE diploma programmes with positive employment outcomes and salaries comparable to that of polytechnic graduates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE will also double the TD programmes, offering six TDs, up from three today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A total of 1,400 places will be offered across ITE diploma programmes, enabling more than 10% of ITE Nitec and Higher Nitec graduates to progress through these pathways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One student who has benefited is Izz, who enrolled in the Nitec in Space Design (Architecture) before progressing to the Higher Nitec in Architectural Technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Izz interned at an architectural firm as part of his Higher Nitec course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The firm was so impressed by him and his hard work and dedication and decided to sponsor him for his WSDip in Architectural Building Information Modelling (BIM) and Design while concurrently employing him as an architectural assistant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has allowed Izz to directly apply what he has learnt in class and work to client projects, giving him a head start in his career.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With these enhancements, we hope to better support the needs of diverse student profiles, their aspirations and strengthen their career readiness and resilience for jobs of the future economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, we would also like to take this opportunity to assure Mr Leon Perera that internship is an important feature of our polytechnic and ITE education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Internships allow students to apply what is taught in the classroom to the real world and equip them with deeper industry-ready skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All polytechnics and ITE have made internships a compulsory component of their courses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Institutions also work closely with the industry to offer quality internships to their students, regardless of their socioeconomic backgrounds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, MOE is committed to nurture and develop the potential of students with different needs and strengths.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For students with special educational needs, we will strengthen efforts to nurture inclusivity in schools by deepening partnerships between Special Education schools (SPED) and general education schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It will create more opportunities for interaction and these aim to help students become more inclusive and thoughtful towards others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise that it is not easy to nurture students with special educational needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, we will continue our efforts to improve the teaching and learning in SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also channel more resources to SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from SPED schools, we will also make improvements in the polytechnic and ITE sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a major change in our education system landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
